command: dcctl install
flags: 38

--alert-config
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: use this Alertmanager configuration file as it is, for receivers beyond webhook and email (Slack, PagerDuty, OpsGenie, Teams...). It replaces what --alert-webhook and --alert-email would build, so route the Watchdog alert inside it; dcctl checks that it parses and that every route names a receiver it defines

--alert-email
  type: stringSlice
  default: "[]"
  repeatable: true
  usage: send alerts to this address (repeatable). Needs --alert-smtp-host and --alert-smtp-from

--alert-smtp-from
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: sender address for --alert-email

--alert-smtp-host
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: SMTP server for --alert-email, as host:port (for example smtp.example.com:587)

--alert-smtp-password-file
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: read the SMTP password from this file, so it never appears in the process list or shell history

--alert-smtp-user
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: SMTP user for --alert-email. Needs --alert-smtp-password-file

--alert-watchdog-webhook
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: send the always-firing Watchdog alert to this URL, every minute, so a dead-man's-switch service (Healthchecks, Dead Man's Snitch, Cronitor) tells you when the alerting pipeline itself goes silent. Without it a broken Alertmanager looks exactly like a healthy, quiet cluster

--alert-webhook
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: send alerts to this webhook URL (Alertmanager's webhook format, which Slack-compatible relays, PagerDuty, Opsgenie and most incident tools accept). Every alert the platform raises is dropped without a receiver. The URL is a credential and is kept in a Secret, never in the infrastructure state. Naming any --alert-* flag restates ALL the routing

--allow-legacy-db-removal
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: proceed even though this cluster still runs the pre-CloudNativePG relational StatefulSet (dc-postgresql). 🔴 This ASSERTS THAT YOU HAVE HANDLED THE DATA — applying with it set destroys that StatefulSet and brings up an empty database on the same hostname

--aws-nlb
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: EKS: which ingress controllers' LoadBalancer Services get an AWS Network Load Balancer (service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: nlb) instead of the Classic one a plain Service gets: traefik, nginx, all, or none (turns it off). Only a Network Load Balancer passes the client's address through, which the per-source rate limits and the trusted-proxy rule depend on. Left off, each controller's Service keeps what it has. A value that CHANGES an existing Service replaces its load balancer and so changes the hostname clients resolve: repoint DNS afterwards (the install says so). traefik alone leaves ingress-nginx's Service as it is, for a cluster mid-cutover

--backup-credentials-file
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: send database backups to an object store you already own, described by this JSON file: {endpointUrl, bucketRdb, bucketTsdb, accessKeyId, secretAccessKey}. Without it the cluster provisions its own in-cluster store, which lives in the same failure domain as the databases it backs up. Keep the file readable only by you

--backup-snapshot-class
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: take each database's daily base backup as a CSI volume snapshot with this VolumeSnapshotClass instead of a full copy in the backup store. A full copy still goes to the store weekly, WAL archiving is unchanged, and restores still read the store. The class must exist, use deletionPolicy Delete, and belong to the driver that provisions the database volumes. Every instance on the cluster follows it

--build
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: developer path: ko-build the operator image from this source checkout and push it to a local registry, instead of pulling a published one. Builds ONLY the operator; the service images are an instance's and are built by dcctl bootstrap --build

--clear-alert-routing
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: remove the alert routing: alerts go back to no receiver and the instance reports ALERTS NOT ROUTED

--cluster
  type: string
  default: "devicechain"
  usage: local provider: the kind cluster to create or use

--compact
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: small-footprint preset for the cluster and every instance on it: smaller volumes, lowered JetStream/KV ceilings and scheduling requests, no monitoring stack, and — unless --no-tls=false — no cert-manager and therefore no database backups. Instances on a compact cluster keep the default profile or a smaller one

--database-node-selector
  type: stringSlice
  default: "[]"
  repeatable: true
  usage: run the databases only on nodes with this label, as key=value (repeatable; every label must match). Applies to the relational store and to the event store of every instance bootstrapped on the cluster. Refused when too few schedulable nodes match

--database-toleration
  type: stringSlice
  default: "[]"
  repeatable: true
  usage: let the databases run on nodes with this taint, written as kubectl taint writes it: key=value:Effect, or key:Effect for any value (repeatable). Needs --database-node-selector

--dev
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: local-developer preset: --build --yes (builds the operator image from this source checkout); rejects contradictory flags

--dry-run
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: print what would happen without applying changes

--ha
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: a replicated relational store (3 CloudNativePG instances, synchronous), and every instance bootstrapped on this cluster HA too: a 3-server NATS cluster with replicated streams and a replicated event store. Needs at least 3 schedulable nodes; database volumes are sized per instance

--help
  shorthand: -h
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  annotation cobra_annotation_flag_set_by_cobra: ["true"]
  usage: help for install

--kube-context
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: install into this existing cluster instead of a local kind cluster (never created or deleted by dcctl)

--max-connections
  type: int
  default: "0"
  usage: the relational store's connection budget (default 700 on a first install, and what the cluster has on a re-run). Each instance reserves (its relational services x 40) of it when bootstrapped; the default admits two default-profile instances

--mqtt-gateway
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: open TCP 8883 on the ingress controller (Traefik) so an instance can serve MQTT over TLS to devices outside the cluster through its Gateway (dcctl bootstrap|upgrade --mqtt-exposure gateway). It publishes a NEW port on the controller's load balancer, so it is off unless asked for. The broker terminates TLS itself; the controller passes the connection through by SNI. Left off, the install keeps whatever the controller's Service has; --mqtt-gateway=false closes it

--no-cnpg
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: skip the CloudNativePG operator and the database backup plugin — for a cluster that ALREADY runs CNPG, since Helm cannot adopt objects another installer created

--no-monitoring
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: skip the monitoring stack (Prometheus/Grafana); instances on the cluster render no ServiceMonitors or alerts

--no-tls
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: with --compact: instances serve plain HTTP, so cert-manager is not installed and database backups (whose plugin needs it) are off. --compact --no-tls=false keeps both

--output
  shorthand: -o
  type: string
  default: "text"
  usage: output format: text (the output dcctl has always printed) or json (the install's events, one JSON object per line on stdout and nothing else there, for automation; it never reads stdin, so a confirmation is given with --yes or the run is refused before it changes anything)

--registry
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: pull the operator image from this registry (default: the published registry, or the local one with --build)

--relational-store-max-wal-mib
  type: int
  default: "0"
  usage: relational store max_wal_size soft checkpoint target in MiB (0: stock default; positive: at least 64). Omitted keeps the recorded choice, or the root default on a first install. Recorded before apply; limited to a quarter of storage by the root

--remove-legacy-ingress
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: remove ingress-nginx from a cluster that still runs it. An install otherwise leaves it serving and installs Traefik beside it. Refused while any Ingress object in the cluster still names its class (each instance must first be moved with 'dcctl upgrade --drop-legacy-ingress'); on a local cluster Traefik takes the node's ports 80 and 443 in the same apply

--restore-rdb-at
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: stop the relational store's recovery at this RFC3339 timestamp instead of replaying the whole archive. For the disaster where the data was destroyed correctly — a bad migration, a mistaken delete — so pick a moment strictly before the damage. Needs --restore-rdb-from

--restore-rdb-from
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: disaster recovery: recover the RELATIONAL store from this archive path (the serverName inside the backup bucket, e.g. dc-rdb) instead of initialising an empty database. 🔴 Only takes effect when the store is CREATED — recover by installing into a cluster whose relational store is not there, not by re-running against a live one

--size
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: cluster size: base (the default) or compact, which is the same as --compact. The perf sizes are chosen per instance with dcctl bootstrap --size

--skip-preflight
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: skip the local-system preflight checks

--version
  type: string
  default: ""
  usage: install the operator at this released tag (default: the release this dcctl was built for). This is the CLUSTER's version — the instances on it carry their own

--yes
  shorthand: -y
  type: bool
  default: "false"
  no-value default: "true"
  usage: assume yes for prompts
